verdicts.reasoning: Every item requires the pupil to produce a numerical result rather than recall one -- "If they put all their leashes together, how many leashes do they have in all?" (seed 11). The four options are near-neighbours (seed 23: "17 / 28 / 19 / 18"), so guessing by elimination is not available.

Seven of ten are genuine situational problems with actors, objects and a combining action -- "There are 4 volleyballs in one basket and 2 volleyballs in another basket" (seed 118). Seeds 57, 91, 127 are bare procedural prompts, computation exercises rather than problems.
verdicts.action_taken: Left registered. The 3/10 counting-on drills are recorded as an open content item.

verdicts.reasoning: All ten items combine two quantities into a total, by aggregation or by counting on -- "Start at 3. Count up 16 more." (seed 91). Both are recognised Grade-1 addition structures under MATATAG.

The ten sums are 6, 18, 5, 15, 11, 9, 19, 19, 6, 13 -- all within 20, with no breach of the ceiling. The spread genuinely exercises the range rather than clustering: four sums sit below 10, three in the teens, and three reach 18-19, so the top of the band is tested.
